subject: maths
title: Double-Angle Identities and R-form
welcome_lead: Manipulate trig identities and convert sums to single sines with R-form.
meta_desc: Maths adventure on double-angle identities and a sin θ + b cos θ = R sin(θ + α).
final_note: R = √(a^2 + b^2), tan α = b/a - the R-form duo!

concepts.def: cos 2θ = cos^2 θ - sin^2 θ = 1 - 2sin^2 θ.
a sin θ + b cos θ = R sin(θ + α).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Solve sin 2x = sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π.

2 sin x cos x - sin x = 0, sin x (2 cos x - 1) = 0. x = 0, π, π/3, 5π/3.

Express 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ as R sin(θ + α).

R = √(9+16) = 5, tan α = 4/3, α ≈ 53.1°. So 5 sin(θ + 53.1°).

Show cos 2θ = 1 - 2 sin^2 θ.

cos 2θ = cos^2 θ - sin^2 θ = (1 - sin^2 θ) - sin^2 θ = 1 - 2sin^2 θ.
